1.title: The Scrum Master
1.text: Welcome to Module 5: The Scrum Master. This is the role the exam is named after. You will learn the two accountabilities, the three audiences the Scrum Master serves, what the role is not, and how to choose the best action in a situation. This module is in two parts.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. State the Scrum Master's two accountabilities. Describe how the Scrum Master serves the team, the Product Owner and the organization. Give three scenarios where the Scrum Master leads. Give three ways to support the Product Owner. Say what the Scrum Master is not. And pick the best action in a situation, which is what situational questions test.

1.title: Case Check-In: Reports and Assignments
1.text: You are the Scrum Master at RideLoop, and two requests land on your desk. Grace Whitfield asks for a weekly report on each Developer's progress, and wants you to assign the tasks to speed things up. At the same time, the Developers, tired of planning, ask you to decide who does what. Both requests sound reasonable, but you are accountable for Scrum and the team's effectiveness, not for either request. This module explains why, and what to do instead.

1.title: The Role at a Glance
1.text: The Scrum Master has two accountabilities: establishing Scrum, and the Scrum Team's effectiveness. The Guide calls Scrum Masters true leaders who serve the team and the larger organization. They serve three audiences, as the diagram shows: the Scrum Team, the Product Owner, and the organization. And notice what is missing. The Scrum Master is not accountable for product value, the Sprint plan, quality, or a delivery date.

1.title: Accountability 1: Establishing Scrum
1.text: The first accountability is "establishing Scrum as defined in the Scrum Guide." That means the roles, events, artifacts, commitments and the rules that bind them. The method is to help everyone grasp both the theory and the practice of Scrum, inside the team and across the organization. The means are teaching and coaching, not policing. Part of the job is showing people what a dropped event, or a weak Definition of Done, really costs them. Remember from Module 1: Scrum is immutable, and partial Scrum is not Scrum.

1.title: Accountability 2: The Team's Effectiveness
1.text: The second accountability is the team's effectiveness. The Scrum Master enables the team to improve its practices, always within the Scrum framework. Effectiveness is about the team, not about each person's output. And it rules out a whole family of wrong answers: when a problem appears, the fix is never to add a role, an event or an artifact that Scrum does not have. A project manager, a hardening Sprint, or an extra approval meeting is wrong.

1.title: Serving the Scrum Team
1.text: How does the Scrum Master serve the Scrum Team? In four ways. Coach the members in self-management and cross-functionality. Help the team focus on valuable Increments that meet the Definition of Done. Cause the removal of impediments to progress. And ensure that every event takes place, is worthwhile, and ends on time. Notice the verbs cause and ensure. They make the Scrum Master accountable for the result, but not for doing all the work personally.

1.title: Serving the Product Owner
1.text: How does the Scrum Master serve the Product Owner? The Guide gives four ways, and the learning objective asks for at least three. Offer techniques for the Product Goal and the Product Backlog. Help the team see why clear, concise items matter. Support empirical planning, which means planning from what has happened and adjusting each Sprint. And facilitate stakeholder collaboration when asked or needed: set up conversations, and make the Review a working session. The examples on this slide go beyond the Guide. What the Scrum Master never does: order the Product Backlog or set the Product Goal.

1.title: Serving the Organization
1.text: The third audience is the organization. The Scrum Master leads, trains and coaches the organization as it adopts Scrum. The Scrum Master plans and advises Scrum rollouts, which means advising, not managing the teams that adopt it. The Scrum Master helps people outside the team understand an empirical approach to complex work: transparency, inspection and adaptation. And the Scrum Master removes barriers between stakeholders and Scrum Teams, clearing what blocks them from working together. This is why the role reaches managers, stakeholders and other teams.

1.title: A True Leader Who Serves
1.text: The Guide describes Scrum Masters as true leaders who serve. Leadership here comes from service, influence and example, not from authority. The Scrum Master is neither a boss nor an assistant who does whatever anyone asks. The earlier edition used the word servant-leader; the meaning is the same. In the exam, reject answers that command, and equally reject answers that do nothing. The right answer sits between them.

1.title: Leading in Practice
1.text: The learning objective asks for three scenarios where the Scrum Master leads. The Guide does not list them, so these go beyond it. Pressure to cut quality: model courage and openness. A team that is stuck or in conflict: facilitate, and coach self-management. Improvements that stall in the Retrospectives: help the team pick one change and act on it. Managers who interfere: lead the conversation about working through the Product Owner. And an organization adopting Scrum: train, coach and advise.

1.title: What the Scrum Master Is Not
1.text: Now what the Scrum Master is not. Not the team's manager who assigns tasks, because the team is self-managing and there is no hierarchy. Not a project manager, because Scrum has none. Not the Product Owner's assistant, and not the one who orders the Product Backlog. Not required to run every event or to attend the Daily Scrum. Not the only person who removes impediments. And not able to cancel a Sprint. That is the Product Owner's authority alone.

1.title: The Scrum Master in the Events
1.text: Where does the Scrum Master appear in the events? Across the whole Sprint, the Scrum Master makes sure every event happens, adds value, and ends on time. In Sprint Planning, a member of the team. At the Daily Scrum, not required: it is the Developers' event, and the Scrum Master takes part only as a Developer if actively working on Sprint Backlog items. At the Review, a member who facilitates stakeholder collaboration as needed. At the Retrospective, a member whose accountability is the team's effectiveness.

2.title: Situations and Best Actions (1)
2.text: Part two is about situations. Here are common ones with the best action. They go beyond the Guide, but they follow from it. A blocker the team cannot remove: make it visible, and work with the right people to clear it fast. A manager asks who works on what, as Grace did: explain self-management, and point to the Sprint Backlog. The Product Owner adds work mid-Sprint: help negotiate scope without endangering the Sprint Goal. The team wants to skip the Retrospective: explain what is lost. The Product Backlog is vague: offer techniques.

2.title: Situations and Best Actions (2)
2.text: More situations. Again, they go beyond the Guide. Stakeholders skip the Review: help the Product Owner and the team engage them. The team wants to relax the Definition of Done: remind them that quality does not decrease, and unfinished work is not part of the Increment. Developers disagree on a design: facilitate, because the Developers decide. The team asks you to decide who does what, as the RideLoop Developers did: coach the team to decide. A manager wants an event skipped: explain what the event is for, and what the organization loses. Other teams want Scrum: lead, train and coach, and advise on the rollout.

2.title: Best and Wrong Answer Patterns
2.text: You can often choose by pattern. Best answers serve, coach or facilitate. They make the problem visible, keep Scrum intact, leave decisions with their owners, and act instead of waiting. Wrong answers command or assign work, decide for the team, add roles or events, or do nothing. Absolute words like never and always are a warning, but check the Guide before rejecting one. Only the Product Owner cancels a Sprint is a real rule. These patterns come from practice, not from the Guide.

2.title: Three Accountabilities Compared
2.text: Compare the three accountabilities once more. The Scrum Master is accountable for Scrum and the team's effectiveness. The Product Owner is accountable for the value of the product and for Product Backlog management. The Developers are accountable for the Sprint plan, quality, daily adaptation and mutual accountability. And how the work is done is decided by the Developers. When an option moves a decision to the wrong person, it is wrong.

2.title: Traps: What the Exam Expects
2.text: Here are the traps. Serve and lead; do not command or manage. But do not be passive either: act when the team cannot solve a problem. Ensure and cause mean accountable for the result. Only the Product Owner cancels a Sprint. Improve within Scrum; do not add a project manager, a hardening Sprint or an approval gate. Watch the old wording: servant-leader and Development Team. And the Scrum Master may work on Sprint Backlog items, then joins the Daily Scrum as a Developer.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Recap. The Scrum Master is accountable for Scrum and for the team's effectiveness. The role serves the team, the Product Owner and the organization. It leads through service, influence and example. Decisions stay with their owners. The Daily Scrum is the Developers' event. And the best answer serves, makes the problem visible, keeps Scrum intact, and acts. Now test yourself.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. At the Daily Scrum, Ben reports that the shared payment test environment run by Ravi's Platform Team has been down for two days, and the Developers have no authority to fix it. What is the best action for the Scrum Master? The four options are on the screen. Choose your answer. The answer is C. The Scrum Master is accountable for causing the removal of impediments, which can mean working with others in the organization. Leaving the team alone gives that up, and waiting for the Retrospective delays the fix.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. Several stakeholders have started giving work directly to individual RideLoop Developers during the Sprint, and the Sprint Goal is at risk. What is the best action for the Scrum Master? The four options are on the screen. Choose your answer. The answer is B. The Product Backlog is the single source of work, and those who want it changed convince the Product Owner. The Scrum Master helps stakeholders understand this. A ban on contact is wrong, and only the Product Owner can cancel a Sprint.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. Wei and Tomas disagree about the design of a feature and ask the Scrum Master to make the final decision. What is the best action? The four options are on the screen. Choose your answer. The answer is D. How the work is done is at the Developers' sole discretion, so the Scrum Master facilitates and the Developers decide. The Product Owner does not decide the design either, and escalating adds a hierarchy.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. What are the Scrum Master's two accountabilities? The four options are on the screen. Choose your answer. The answer is A: establishing Scrum as defined in the Guide, and the Scrum Team's effectiveness. Value and the Product Backlog belong to the Product Owner, the Sprint plan and quality to the Developers, and managing tasks is not part of the role at all.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. Which list contains ways the Scrum Master serves the Product Owner? The four options are on the screen. Choose your answer. The answer is B: finding techniques for the Product Goal and the Product Backlog, and facilitating stakeholder collaboration. Ordering and the Product Goal belong to the Product Owner, selection to the Developers, and the last option describes serving the organization.

2.title: Answers at a Glance
2.text: Here are all five answers together. Question one: C. Cause the removal of the impediment, with others when needed. Question two: B. Stakeholders influence the work through the Product Owner. Question three: D. The Developers decide how. Question four: A. Establishing Scrum, and the team's effectiveness. Question five: B. Techniques and stakeholder collaboration. That completes Module 5. Next, Module 6 covers the Sprint and the Scrum events.
